trigger: User authorized the experiment after the terrain product-identity PASS; no further data-validity work is in scope.
question: Does the official pretrained NASA encoder give a better frozen-feature Geology probe than an identically initialized random encoder on the fixed Moonstone Train/Val cohort?

arms: pretrained: official base encoder with the verified checkpoint, strictly loaded
random: identical architecture and head/adapters from the same seed, no pretrained weights
design.encoder_gradients: none; encoder weights and buffers are never updated
design.feature: encoder token sequence, mean-pooled over tokens, exactly the mean-pool that TerrainTransfer.forward applies
design.head: single Linear(out_channels, 49), identical initialization across arms
design.normalization: audited NASA config via prepare_terrain; raw physical metres and degrees

budget.epoch_permutation: torch.randperm with Generator().manual_seed(seed + epoch), identical across arms

acceptance_gates: Both arms use the same cohort, batch order, head initialization and budget

Cached features must match a fresh-process recomputation within 1e-3 absolute, with bitwise identity recorded as a diagnostic; measured cross-process differences reach 1.5e-4 against features whose mean absolute value is 0.28 (pretrained) and 0.77 (random)
Cached-feature logits must match a direct model forward on the same samples
Encoder state digest must be unchanged after head training
No Test ID is constructed, read or scored
reported_metrics: val macro-F1 over the full 49 classes
mean and sample standard deviation over the three seeds (never a confidence interval)
claims_permitted: A paired frozen-feature probe result on the fixed cohort under the declared limitation
If pretrained minus random exceeds the seed-to-seed spread, a first positive transfer signal for this probe only
claims_not_permitted: Full fine-tuning, LoRA or any trained-encoder result
Test performance, new-class capability, landing safety or global lunar conclusions
provenance_limitation: Terrain equals the published Moonstone product bitwise (reports/p3_3_mmap_terrain_linkage.md); the upstream ingestion and interpolation provenance remain the publisher's declaration and are accepted explicitly here.
runtime: private Python3.12.9, torch2.12.1+rocm7.2, RX7900XT gfx1100, deterministic algorithms, no network
training: authorized for the frozen head only

revision_log.change: Cached-feature acceptance moved from bitwise to an absolute bound before any head was trained, after measuring cross-process kernel nondeterminism (random 4.8e-7, pretrained up to 1.5e-4; feature scale mean-abs 0.28-0.77, max 3.8). The 1e-3 bound is set from measurement before scores were observed.
